visual_action: The video shows a clip from a congressional hearing. Senator Bernie Sanders, seated at a dais, questions a man identified as Mr. Bessent, who is seated at a witness table. The camera cuts between shots of Sanders speaking and Bessent listening and then responding.

cast.name: Bernie Sanders
cast.evidence: He is shown speaking throughout the video, and a nameplate in front of him reads 'MR. SANDERS'.

cast.name: Scott Bessent
cast.evidence: He is shown responding to Bernie Sanders' questions, and a nameplate in front of him reads 'MR. BESSENT'.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: The on-screen text at the beginning of the video refers to the person being questioned as 'this Trump appointee'.

on_screen_text.text: Wow... Look at what this Trump appointee just admitted 🤯😬
WHO ARE MAKING LESS THAN $15 AN HOUR,
$7.25 AN HOUR. WILL YOU WORK WITH THOSE
OF US WHO WANT TO RAISE
TO A LIVING WAGE TO TAKE
MILLIONS OF AMERICANS OUT OF POVERTY?
SENATOR, I BELIEVE THAT THE MINIMUM WAGE
IS MORE OF A STATEWIDE AND REGIONAL ISSUE.
SO YOU DON'T THINK WE SHOULD

spoken_summary: Bernie Sanders states that millions of Americans earn low wages and that the federal minimum wage has been stagnant at $7.25 an hour since 2009. He asks Scott Bessent if he will work with them to raise the federal minimum wage to a living wage. Bessent responds that he believes the minimum wage is a state and regional issue. When Sanders asks for clarification, "So you don't think we should change the federal minimum wage of $7.25 an hour?" Bessent replies, "No, sir."
audio_music: The audio consists entirely of spoken dialogue from the congressional hearing, without any background music or sound effects.
editing_pacing: The editing consists of simple cuts between two static shots of the speakers (talking heads) in a hearing room.
central_claim: A Trump appointee, Scott Bessent, stated in a congressional hearing that he does not support raising the federal minimum wage.
intended_effect: To generate disapproval of Scott Bessent and Donald Trump's position on the federal minimum wage.
